investigations.name: arm1-monolithic-tellurium
investigations.description: Methods arm of the SBML-decomposition investigation on Teusink glycolysis (BIOMD0000000064, 17 floating species). The model is authored as inline Antimony and shown in the Model tab. Arm 1 hands the entire model to libroadrunner/CVODE in one piece — fast, numerically exact, but opaque and uncomposable.
investigations.title: Arm 1 — Monolithic Tellurium (reference)
investigations.objective: Does the whole SBML model, integrated in one libroadrunner/CVODE call through a single TelluriumProcess, reproduce the model's reference trajectory, and what is its performance baseline?
investigations.claim: Monolithic Tellurium reproduces the reference to ~1e-6 and is the fastest arm — the speed + accuracy reference.

investigations.name: arm2-operator-split
investigations.description: Methods arm of the SBML-decomposition investigation on Teusink glycolysis (BIOMD0000000064, 17 floating species). The model is authored as inline Antimony and shown in the Model tab. A MECHANICAL split (not a biological seam): a Lie split into complementary reaction groups sharing a species store each coupling interval.
investigations.title: Arm 2 — Operator-split Tellurium
investigations.objective: If the same model is advanced in operator-split sub-steps that exchange state through a vivarium store each coupling interval, how much orchestration overhead and splitting error does that add, and does the error shrink with the interval?
investigations.claim: Operator-splitting error is real and shrinks with the coupling interval (0.587 → 0.067); a clean split was only possible across the weakly-coupled glycogen/trehalose sinks — splitting across the strong P/ATP/ADP energy coupling diverges.

investigations.name: arm3-modular-submodels
investigations.description: Methods arm of the SBML-decomposition investigation on Teusink glycolysis (BIOMD0000000064, 17 floating species). The model is authored as inline Antimony and shown in the Model tab. Two SubmodelProcess nodes (upper/lower glycolysis) + an EnergyStep share ONE species store and reconcile additive deltas through the real bigraph apply/reconcile path.
investigations.title: Arm 3 — Modular submodels (biological seam)
investigations.objective: If the model is partitioned along a biological seam (upper vs lower glycolysis at aldolase/F16P) into two coupled process nodes sharing a store, does it still reproduce the reference, and is this a genuine multi-process composition?
investigations.claim: A biological-seam decomposition reproduces the reference (0.468 → 0.100 as the coupling step shrinks, T=0.15) as a GENUINE multi-process composition — the first point on the spectrum where the model is composable.

investigations.name: arm4-native-pbg
investigations.description: Methods arm of the SBML-decomposition investigation on Teusink glycolysis (BIOMD0000000064, 17 floating species). The model is authored as inline Antimony and shown in the Model tab. The 17 Teusink rate laws + the 3 sqrt assignment rules are hand-ported to pure Python/numpy and integrated with scipy LSODA — no libroadrunner at runtime. Built in two leaf variants (scalar-dict and numpy-array).
investigations.title: Arm 4 — Fully native process-bigraph
investigations.objective: Can the glycolysis ODE network be reimplemented as native process-bigraph processes (no libroadrunner at runtime) at reference fidelity, and does the state leaf representation (scalar-dict vs numpy-array) matter for performance at this scale?
investigations.claim: A fully native process-bigraph implementation reaches reference fidelity (~1e-7); at 17 species the scalar-dict-vs-array leaf choice is perf-irrelevant (only bites at 100s-1000s of species).

investigations.name: arm5-ensemble-ray
investigations.description: Methods arm of the SBML-decomposition investigation on Teusink glycolysis (BIOMD0000000064, 17 floating species). The model is authored as inline Antimony and shown in the Model tab. Arm 5 runs N monolithic instances concurrently via Ray OS processes (the baseline composite is one monolithic instance; the ensemble is N of them with parameter draws).
investigations.title: Arm 5 — Ensemble on Ray
investigations.objective: When many instances of the monolithic model are run as a parameter ensemble, does vivarium orchestration on a real parallel backend (Ray) deliver a genuine throughput speedup?
investigations.claim: A Ray ensemble of monoliths gives a real 7.5x wall-clock speedup on 16 cores — the one arm where vivarium wins on speed; libroadrunner does NOT release the GIL, so in-process threads cannot (they backfire).

investigations.name: arm6-coupling-demo
investigations.description: Methods arm of the SBML-decomposition investigation on Teusink glycolysis (BIOMD0000000064, 17 floating species). The model is authored as inline Antimony and shown in the Model tab. Arm 6 swaps arm 3's lower-glycolysis submodel for the native-pbg process while upper stays libroadrunner, both sharing one store. This is the composability existence proof; it has no monolithic reference (accuracy-exempt).
investigations.title: Arm 6 — Cross-engine coupling demonstration
investigations.objective: Can a single composite run part of the model in libroadrunner and part as a native process, sharing one store — a composition a monolithic SBML model structurally cannot express?
investigations.claim: A single composite runs HALF in libroadrunner and HALF native, sharing one store — structurally impossible for a monolith — and reproduces the biological-seam arm to 3.2e-7. This is the composability payoff, not a numeric result.

investigations.name: arm7-multirate
investigations.description: Methods arm of the SBML-decomposition investigation. Unlike arms 1-6 (equal coupling intervals, the cheap regime), arm 7 deliberately builds N INDEPENDENT arm-1 monolithic glycolysis instances (bulk-bound TelluriumProcess), each advanced on a DIFFERENT geometrically-spaced interval (fastest -> slowest, the slow tail overrunning the run horizon). The instances share no store and are uncoupled, so there is no operator-splitting error — each is just the arm-1 monolith on its own clock. The composite is run under scheduler="scan" (stock O(P^2) tick loop) and scheduler="heap" (#270's event-min-heap, O(P log P)); the Task-4 timing harness times run() alone (construction excluded) for P in {4,16,64,128,256}.
investigations.title: Arm 7 — Multi-rate scheduler stress test (process-bigraph
investigations.objective: When a composite is genuinely multi-rate (many independent instances each on a different coupling interval — the mismatched-interval case arms 1-6 avoid), does process-bigraph #270's event-heap scheduler reduce the per-tick O(P) due-scan to O(log P), so the many-rate run scales as ~O(P log P) instead of O(P^2) — and does it stay bit-identical to the stock scan loop?
investigations.claim: process-bigraph #270's event-heap scheduler is bit-identical to the stock scan loop (same math, different tick order) and its wall-clock advantage grows monotonically with P on a genuinely multi-rate composite — measured 0.98x at P=4 (heap bookkeeping with nothing to gain), crossing over near P~50-64, to 1.64x at P=256 on real libroadrunner/CVODE instances. The per-process CVODE integration dominates the per-tick scan until P reaches the low hundreds, so the multiplier is modest at the P a unit test can afford; it is reported as measured, and the regime where it grows large (hundreds-to-thousands of cheap processes) is #270's own 4.8x@P=100 -> 46x@P=1000 micro-benchmark, cited not reproduced.

investigations.name: arm8-multiorgan
investigations.description: Methods arm of the SBML-decomposition investigation. A synthetic multi-organ "body" is the scaling knob: N organ compartments, each a small 3-species enzymatic chain (o{i}_G -> o{i}_M -> o{i}_P), every one drawing from and returning to a SINGLE shared plasma metabolite Glc_blood (uptake + release flux), so the organs are genuinely coupled through the shared pool and the body is a closed, mass- conserving system that relaxes to a finite steady state at any N. Species = 3N+1, reactions = 4N. Two implementations run the SAME body: (1) MONOLITHIC — the whole N-organ model as one Antimony string integrated by a single libroadrunner/CVODE instance (build_multiorgan_antimony, on the generator's config.model so the Model page shows it); (2) DECOMPOSED — N OrganProcess nodes, each its own small libroadrunner instance built from that organ's 4 reactions, all sharing ONE blood store into which each writes its per-interval Glc_blood delta; the deltas reconcile additively through the bigraph apply path (exactly arm 3's shared-store coupling). multiorgan_scaling records, per N, BOTH halves of BOTH implementations — mono_build_s + mono_run_s (= mono_total_s) and decomp_build_s + decomp_run_s (= decomp_total_s) — plus accuracy (decomposed vs monolithic max_rel_err). The decomposed run is measured through N=128; N>=256 are build-only anchors (the decomposed pbg run is too slow for the harness there, and is left honestly unmeasured rather than guessed).
investigations.title: Arm 8 — Multi-organ scaling (where monolithic Tellurium strains)
investigations.objective: As an SBML model grows large (tens -> hundreds -> thousands of species), where does a monolithic libroadrunner/CVODE instance strain — in model BUILD (compile) time, in integration time, or both — and does decomposing the body into N per-organ process-bigraph sub-processes coupled through a shared store actually come out ahead end-to-end, or does it just move the cost around?
investigations.claim: The one strong, well-measured result is that the MONOLITHIC libroadrunner BUILD strains superlinearly in the reaction count: 0.20 s at 97 species -> 1.76 s at 385 -> 5.54 s at 769 -> 18.5 s at 1537 species (~94x for ~16x the reactions, ~O(N^1.64)), with the dense-CVODE run blowing up alongside it (0.0023 s -> 2.56 s). That is the real strain point and the reason a very large SBML model is painful to run monolithically. Decomposition is NOT a free win: building N small models is SLOWER than the single compile up to ~100 species (1.7x slower at 97 species), reaches only rough parity at 385 species (1.40 vs 1.76 s) and becomes a clear build win only at ~1500 species (2.4x); and the decomposed per-tick RUN overhead is ~16x the monolith's CVODE run, so the decomposed body is SLOWER END-TO-END at every N measured (decomp_total 2.35 s vs mono_total 1.81 s at 385 species). The end-to-end gap narrows with N but the decomposed run is unmeasured past N=128, so no end-to-end crossover is claimed. Decomposition is a structural trade — it swaps the monolith's superlinear build for much higher run overhead — that would only pay off end-to-end on models larger than measured. CRUCIAL caveat: the additive-split accuracy is good only at small N / fine interval (max_rel_err 2e-3 at N=2, 1.2e-2 at N=8, 5.2e-2 at N=32) and is 0.31 (31%) at N=128 — so the regime where the speed gap narrows and the regime of acceptable accuracy do NOT co-occur at a fixed coupling interval. All numbers measured, not fabricated.

investigations.name: arm9-abm-meanfield
investigations.description: The adversarial / ablation arm of the SBML-decomposition investigation: the case built to BREAK the naive "any model is an SBML model" claim that arms 1-8 implicitly rest on. The SAME Lotka-Volterra predator-prey system is realised two ways. (1) THE ABM — a well-mixed population of DISCRETE individuals (integer prey/predator counts) whose prey birth (propensity r*X), predation (a/K*X*Y), predator birth (b/K*X*Y) and predator death (m*Y) are STOCHASTIC EVENTS, advanced by the exact Gillespie SSA (direct method) in a native process-bigraph PredatorPreyABMProcess. There is no continuous RHS for CVODE; one run is one stochastic realisation, so an ensemble is needed for statistics. This model is NOT an SBML model. (2) THE MEAN-FIELD REDUCTION — the deterministic Lotka-Volterra ODE (dx/dt = r*x - a*x*y, dy/dt = b*x*y - m*y) as Antimony integrated by libroadrunner/CVODE in a TelluriumProcess, carried on the predator_prey_meanfield generator's config.model so the Model page shows exactly what the SBML reduction is. The 1/K system-size factor on the quadratic propensities makes the density X/K obey the same scale-free ODE at every K, so K is a clean knob from "stochastic handful of individuals" (K=8) to "effectively continuous" (K=400). abm_ensemble measures, per scale, the SSA ensemble mean/variance + extinction fraction; the finding compares the mean (in density units) to the ODE. Nothing is tuned to make the ABM match the ODE — the small-K divergence is the point.
investigations.title: Arm 9 — Agent-based model vs its mean-field SBML reduction (the adversarial arm)
investigations.objective: The whole investigation assumes the model you start with is an SBML/ODE network. But can an AGENT-BASED model — a population of discrete individuals with stochastic interactions — even BE an SBML/Tellurium model? If you reduce it to a mean-field ODE and run it in libroadrunner/CVODE, where does that reduction hold and where does it structurally break?
investigations.claim: An agent-based model reduces to an SBML/Tellurium mean-field ODE ONLY in the large-population, well-mixed, deterministic limit; it structurally cannot capture stochasticity, discreteness, extinction, or individual heterogeneity. MEASURED (Lotka-Volterra, base rates r=a=b=m=1, start density (1.8, 1.0), horizon ~2 periods): at a LARGE population scale K=400 (80 SSA runs) the mean-field ODE reproduces the SSA ensemble mean to a max relative error of 4.9% with 0% of runs going extinct — the reduction is VALID. At a SMALL scale K=8 (200 SSA runs) the ensemble mean diverges from the ODE by 68% max relative error and 94% of runs go EXTINCT before the horizon, hitting an absorbing state (prey or predator count 0) that the neutrally-stable ODE — which simply orbits forever — can never reach. The ODE additionally cannot represent the ensemble variance at ANY K. So "can an ABM be an SBML model?" has an honest, quantified answer: yes, but only as its large-population mean-field limit, and that reduction silently discards exactly the stochastic/discrete phenomena (extinction, demographic noise) that are often the biological point. This breaks the naive "just write it as SBML" claim.
